newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes little changed against US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes little changed against US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed little unchanged at 8.2940 on Friday from Thursday's 8.2939 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai, despite a trade surplus of $1.75 billion in January, dealers said.
Dealers said the death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping was not a factor in the market at all.
The weighted average price on Thursday was 8.2939.
According to official, China posted a trade surplus of $1.75 billion in January this year.
Dealers said that the yuan moved quite stable, with concerns of the central bank's intervention whenever necessary.
The yuan opened higher at 8.2937 and moved around the 8.2940 level for most of the session, hitting an intraday low of 8.2983 and a high of 8.2936. Trading was not active.
"The trade surplus increases the supply of the U.S. dollar, but worries on possible intervention by the central bank curbed its rise," said one dealer. "Buying of the yuan has dropped recently."
Another dealer said there was no intervention from the central bank today but some speculative selling of the yuan emerged late in the session to push the yuan down to around the 8.30 level.
"The selling failed to push the yuan lower than that level due to the general upward pressure on the yuan," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to down to some extent early next week.
The yuan closed down at 6.7388 from 6.7125 against 100 Japanese yen and slightly up at 1.0715 from 1.0720 against the Hong Kong dollar.
